items.title: React: Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution in React Server Components
items.description:
### Impact

Crafted payloads targeting frameworks supporting React Server Components can lead to remote code execution. This only affects extremely rare cases where responses transport multiple typed arrays and an attacker-controlled value.

Updating immediately is recommended.

The vulnerability exists in versions 19.0.0 through 19.0.8, 19.1.0 through 19.1.9, 19.2.0 through 19.2.8 and 19.3.0 of:

- react-server-dom-webpack
- react-server-dom-parcel
- react-server-dom-turbopack

### Patches

Fixes were back ported to versions 19.0.09, 19.1.10, 19.2.9, and 19.3.1.

If applications are using any of the above packages please upgrade to any of the fixed versions immediately.

If an app’s React code does not use a server, the app is not affected by this vulnerability. If an app does not use a framework, bundler, or bundler plugin that supports React Server Components, the app is not affected

items.title: compose-lint: File paths embedded in pull requests can inject CI workflow commands through command-line error messages
items.description:
### Impact

0.31.0 fixed GHSA-6f4g-xm8v-pgv6, where text from a Compose file became GitHub Actions workflow commands in compose-lint's output. The fix escapes the command openers in compose-lint's own output, but not in the argument parser's error messages. items.title: compose-lint: Workflow command injection through SARIF-directory errors triggered by pull request symlinks
items.description:
### Impact

In Action tags v0.30.0 and v0.31.0, when `sarif-file:` names a file in a subdirectory that can't be created, the Action prints the directory's resolved path in an error message. In v0.31.0 that message is outside the window in which the Action turns command processing off, and v0.30.0 has no such window. ## Summary

The Kubeflow Pipelines frontend reflected untrusted pod names and namespaces into HTML error responses from the pod-information and pod-events routes. An attacker could craft a link that causes JavaScript to execute in the frontend's origin when a user follows it and reaches an affected error response.

Affected routes include `/pipeline/k8s/pod` and `/pipeline/k8s/pod/events` (the deployment's configured base path may differ).

## Impact and prerequisites

Successful exploitation requires a victim to open an attacker-supplied link and reach the vulnerable response. JavaScript execution may expose information accessible to the victim's browser or perform actions in the application's origin.
